name: get_screen_height
inputs: none
wrapper: direct (no caller found in ROOT or overlays)
purpose: Returns the constant 200 in AX. All four drivers (EGA/CGA/HER/T1K) return 0xC8, so it is most likely 'number of pixel rows' (or a driver signature). Touches nothing else.
notes: Unused by the game; can be a trivial constant in the port.

name: init
inputs: AX=set_mode flag (nonzero = program the hardware), BX=near pointer (DS-relative, DS=DGROUP) to the graphics config block (DGROUP 0x52ba)
purpose: Stores the config pointer at CS:0x23c (every later entry reads config fields through it: +0x0a clip enable (0x52c4), +0x1a/+0x1c clip ymin/ymax (0x52d4/0x52d6), +0x1e draw page (0x52d8, written by entry 5), +0x24 17-byte palette (0x52de..0x52ee)). If AX!=0: INT 10h AX=000Dh (EGA mode 0Dh, 320x200x16, 4 planes at A000:0000, 40 bytes/row, 8000 bytes/plane), INT 10h AX=1002h with ES:DX=config+0x24 (palette registers 0..15 + overscan; DATA.OVL holds 00 01 02 03 04 05 06 07 38 39 3A 3B 3C 3D 3E 3F 00 = the default EGA colours, i.e. the standard 16-colour CGA/EGA palette, overscan black), INT 10h AH=05h AL=0 (display page 0). First call only (flag CS:0x866): fills the row-offset table CS:0x72[y]=y*40 for y=0..199 and transforms the bit-reverse table at CS:0x314 into t[i]=(bitrev8(i)<<1)|1 (used by the mirrored blit of entry 33). Ends with the standard register reset (GC reg 3 = 0 normal write, SEQ map mask = 0Fh, GC bit mask = FFh).
notes: Does not set up page 1 (entry 2 does). The port needs: config pointer semantics, palette = default EGA 16 colours.

name: init_page1
inputs: none used by EGA (ROOT sets CF=1; CGA/T1K/HER ignore CF too and allocate a DOS block)
outputs: AX=segment of page 1 (0xA800 on EGA; 0 on failure in CGA)
purpose: EGA: sets CS:0x202 (page-1 segment) = 0xA800, then zero-fills 0x4000 words at A800:0000 (32 KB; with the map mask at 0Fh this clears all four planes), resets the GC registers and returns 0xA800. Page 1 is therefore the off-screen half of EGA video RAM (A000:8000..A000:FCFF). Its layout is NOT interleaved like page 0: it is a plane-separated buffer, plane p of the 320x200 image at A800:(p*0x1F40) + y*40 + x/8, and every byte is physically replicated into all four hardware planes so it can be read back with any read-map setting. ROOT then (ab)uses the returned segment as the LZW dictionary (0x1800 words) during every file load, so page 1 contents are destroyed by any file load.
notes: CGA.DRV allocates 0x400 paragraphs (16 KB) with INT 21h/48h instead and returns 0 on failure. Port: page 1 = second 320x200 buffer; file loading must not need it.

name: stub_3
inputs: none
purpose: Jump-table slot points at a bare RETF (shared stub at 3000:0860). Unused.
notes: Entries 3,6,7,11,14,18,23,29 all share this stub.

name: free_page1
inputs: AX=page (only 1 does anything)
purpose: If AX==1 and the page-1 segment (CS:0x202) is nonzero: INT 21h AH=49h with ES=page-1 segment. In CGA/T1K/HER that releases the DOS buffer allocated by entry 2; on EGA the segment is A800 (video RAM), DOS returns an error which is ignored, so it is a no-op. CS:0x202 is not cleared.
notes: Unused by the game.

name: set_draw_page
inputs: AX=page (0 or 1)
purpose: AX==0: config+0x1e (DGROUP 0x52d8) := 0. AX==1 and page-1 segment nonzero: config+0x1e := 1. Any other value is ignored. Entries 13,16,19,20,21,25,27,31,32(CF=1) read this word to choose page 0 (visible, A000) or page 1 (off-screen). Entries 17 (line), 12 (get pixel), 34 (both modes), 35 and 36 ignore it (see their records).

name: stub_6
inputs: none
purpose: Bare RETF stub. Unused.

name: stub_7
inputs: none
purpose: Bare RETF stub. Unused.

name: copy_rect_page1_to_page0
inputs: AX=x1, BX=y1, CX=x2, DX=y2 (inclusive, normalised by ROOT), CF=1: copy page1->page0; CF=0: (intended page0->page1)
purpose: CF=1: copies the pixel rectangle [x1..x2]x[y1..y2] from page 1 to page 0 (FUN_0772 rectangle path): for each row and each plane it copies the left partial byte under bit mask 0x210, the full bytes, and the right partial byte under bit mask 0x211, so edges are pixel-exact. CF=0: FUN_06fc is entered with CF=0 and returns immediately, i.e. page0->page1 rectangle copies are a NO-OP in EGA.DRV (CGA/T1K/HER have the same JC structure, not verified further). Does not depend on the draw page.
notes: Port: implement rect copy page1->page0; treat src=0,dst=1 as a no-op to stay faithful (or implement it if the game relies on it - callers: COMSUBS f4be, DUNGEON 85a6/9db0, INTRO 8770/88ee/8b46, LOOKOBJ b38c, ROOT 3072).

name: copy_page
inputs: AX=src page, BX=dst page; only (1,0) and (0,1) accepted and only when page 1 exists
purpose: (1,0): copies all 32000 bytes of page 1 (plane region p = A800:p*0x1F40) into page 0 plane p (map mask 1,2,4,8). (0,1): for p=0..3 sets read-map-select=p and copies plane p of page 0 to A800:p*0x1F40 with all planes enabled. Whole-screen copy both directions.

name: swap_pages
inputs: AX,BX = (0,1) or (1,0) (both accepted), page 1 must exist
purpose: Exchanges the full contents of page 0 and page 1 row by row: reads the 4 planes of a page-0 row (40 bytes each) into CS:0x272, writes the page-1 row into page 0 (per plane map mask), then writes the saved row into page 1's four plane regions. 200 rows.
notes: Unused by the game.

name: stub_11
inputs: none
purpose: Bare RETF stub. Unused.

name: get_pixel
purpose: Reads the four planes of page 0 (always A000, ignores the draw page) at (x,y) via read-map-select 3..0 and returns the 4-bit colour (plane 3 = bit 3). No clipping.
notes: Unused by the game.

name: scroll_rect
inputs: AX=x1, BX=y1, CX=x2, DX=y2 (inclusive), SI=signed row count: negative = contents move UP by |SI| rows, positive = move DOWN
wrapper: put_char 1000:16ba (SI=-8 on window rect), scroll_window_up 1f4e (dead), scroll_rect_up 71ca / scroll_rect_down 7200 (earthquake)
purpose: GENERIC PATH (AX != 192): n=|SI|. If (y2-y1)-n == 0 no rows are copied. Scroll up: for r = y1+n..y2 copy row r to row r-n (top to bottom); scroll down: for r = y2-n down to y1 copy row r to row r+n. Only the byte span covering x1..x2 is touched, with pixel-exact left/right edge masks (CS:0x210/0x211). Honours the draw page (config+0x1e==1 -> page 1 buffer, else page 0; page-0 writes outside 0..7999 are skipped). Then the vacated strip (rows y2-n+1..y2 for up, y1..y1+n-1 for down, columns x1..x2) is filled with colour 0 by calling entry 21 with CF=0 (current colour CS:0x312 is saved and restored). FAST PATH (AX == 0xC0 = 192, all other registers ignored): hard-coded scroll of the region x=192..319, starting row 96, upward by 8 rows: for 232 (!) rows it copies row r+8 to row r (r = 96.., i.e. continuing through invisible VRAM rows 200..327 - harmless), copying the first byte (x 192..199) plane by plane but the remaining 15 bytes per row with REP MOVSB under map mask 0Fh / bit mask FFh, which on EGA hardware writes the byte of the last selected read plane (plane 3) into ALL four planes: pixels become 15 where the intensity bit was set, else 0. It does not clear the vacated rows (they receive rows 200..207, which are normally zero). This is the path taken by put_char for a window whose left column is cell 24 (x0*8 = 192), i.e. the main message window, where text is white on black so the result is correct.
notes: Port: implement the generic semantics for all cases (correct 4-plane copy + clear with colour 0); do not reproduce the colour-mangling fast path unless pixel-exact emulation of the message window is wanted.

name: stub_14
inputs: none
purpose: Bare RETF stub. Unused.

name: set_color
inputs: AL=colour 0..15 (ROOT masks it)
purpose: Stores AL at CS:0x312, the current drawing colour used by entries 13 (restore), 16, 17, 19, 20, 21.

name: plot_pixel
inputs: AX=x, BX=y, CF=1: XOR mode
outputs: CF=1 if the point was outside 0..319 x 0..199 (nothing drawn)
purpose: Honours the draw page. CF=0: pixel(x,y) := colour. CF=1: pixel ^= colour (page 0: GC function XOR with bit mask = the pixel bit; page 1: software XOR in the plane-separated buffer). Rejected points leave the internal XOR flag CS:0x204 set (harmless: every drawing entry resets it on exit).

name: draw_line
inputs: AX=x1, BX=y1, CX=x2, DX=y2 (inclusive endpoints), CF=1: XOR mode
purpose: Bresenham line ALWAYS drawn on page 0 (ES forced to A000; the draw page is ignored). No clipping in the driver. Exact algorithm: dx=|x2-x1|, dy=|y2-y1|, sx=sign(x2-x1), sy=sign(y2-y1); major=max(dx,dy), minor=min(dx,dy); err=2*minor-major; repeat major+1 times: plot(x,y) (colour or XOR as entry 16); if err<0 { step along the major axis only (x+=sx if dx>=dy else y+=sy); err+=2*minor } else { x+=sx; y+=sy; err+=2*minor-2*major }. Note: when dx==dy the 'shallow' branch is taken (x steps on the major axis).
notes: ROOT normalises nothing here except clipping; endpoints may be in any order.

name: stub_18
inputs: none
purpose: Bare RETF stub. Unused.

name: draw_hline
inputs: AX=x1, BX=y, CX=x2 (any order, inclusive), CF=1: XOR
purpose: Horizontal span min(x1,x2)..max(x1,x2) on row y, colour CS:0x312, honouring the draw page; pixel := colour or pixel ^= colour. Uses the edge-mask span filler (FUN_045c + FUN_04f6 for page 0, FUN_0622 for page 1). No clipping (ROOT clips).

name: draw_vline
inputs: AX=x, BX=y1, DX=y2 (y1<=y2 required), CF=1: XOR; CX ignored
purpose: Plots pixels (x,y) for y=y1..y2 inclusive (one plot_pixel core call per row), colour or XOR, honouring the draw page. If y1>y2 only (x,y1) is drawn. No clipping.

name: fill_rect
inputs: AX=x1, BX=y1, CX=x2, DX=y2 (x order free, y1<=y2 required, inclusive), CF=1: XOR
wrapper: fill_rect 1000:0aa6 (CF=0), fill_rect_xor 0b86 (CF=1), put_char window clear, entry 13 internally
purpose: Fills rows y1..y2, columns min(x1,x2)..max(x1,x2) with the current colour (CF=0: pixel := colour; CF=1 on page 0: pixel ^= colour). Honours the draw page. Quirk: with CF=1 the GC function register is set to XOR before the page is known, so on PAGE 1 the hardware XOR against the latches cancels the software XOR and the result is an opaque fill with the colour (pixel := colour) - and the GC registers are not reset on the page-1 exit. Also 1 row is always drawn even if y2<y1 is passed.
notes: Port: pixel := colour / pixel ^= colour on either page; page-1 XOR fills are not used by the game as far as known (highlight boxes are drawn on page 0).

name: convert_image_file
inputs: BX=segment of a loaded (decompressed) multi-image .16 file; AX=size (ignored)
wrapper: load_image_file 1000:0bae (files: DNG1-3.16, ITEMS.16, MON0-7.16, STORY1-6.16, TEXT.16, END1/2.16, ENDSC.16, CREATE.16, ULTIMA.16, STARTSC.16)
purpose: In-place conversion of every image in the file from the packed .16 layout to the driver's planar layout. File header: u16 count, then count entries of 4 bytes read as (u16 image_offset, u16 ignored) - this covers both the u32-offset files (DNG/STORY/... high word 0) and the ITEMS/MON files whose entries are (u16 image_offset, u16 mask_offset). Entries with offset 0 are skipped. Image = (u16 w, u16 h, h rows). Packed row = bpr = roundup4(ceil(w/2)) bytes, 2 pixels per byte, high nibble = left pixel. Converted row (same bpr bytes, same place): four consecutive bit-planes of bpr/4 bytes each: bytes [0..bpr/4) = plane 0 (colour bit 0), then plane 1, plane 2, plane 3; within a plane byte the MSB is the leftmost of its 8 pixels. (w,h) are left unchanged. The 1-bpp mask images of ITEMS/MON (referenced only by the second word) are NOT touched.
notes: Conversion core FUN_17be converts 4-byte groups to [p0,p1,p2,p3]; FUN_1271 then regroups each row plane-major. CGA.DRV maps entry 22 to a stub (keeps packed data). Port can keep the original packed data and decode at blit time.

name: stub_23
inputs: none
purpose: Bare RETF stub. Unused.

name: load_tileset
inputs: BX=segment of the decompressed TILES.16 (65536 bytes, 512 tiles x 128 bytes, no header), CX=size-1 (0xFFFF for 64 KB = convert the whole segment; otherwise CX+1 bytes), AX=size (ignored)
wrapper: load_picture_file 1000:0ff4 (all callers - INTRO 8b46, FONT e684, DNGLOOK b3c0 - pass "TILES.16")
purpose: Registers BX as the driver's tile segment (CS:0x206, used by entries 27, 32, 34(CF=1), 36, 30) and converts the whole buffer in place: each 4-byte group (8 packed pixels, high nibble first) becomes 4 plane bytes [p0,p1,p2,p3] (MSB = leftmost pixel, plane k = colour bit k). Resulting tile format: tile t at offset t*0x80; row r (0..15) at +r*8 = [p0L p1L p2L p3L p0R p1R p2R p3R] where L = pixels 0-7 and R = pixels 8-15 of the row.
notes: Because entry 30 frees this segment, the game reloads TILES.16 after big picture sequences (FONT/DNGLOOK callers).

name: draw_image
inputs: AX=segment of a file converted by entry 22, BX=image index, SI=x (pixels; only x>>3 is used, i.e. x is rounded down to a multiple of 8), DI=y, CX=flags: bit0 = vertical flip, bit1 = horizontal mirror (set by entry 33)
wrapper: draw_image 1000:0d4c (CX=mode; 0 nearly everywhere, DUNGEON passes flags) and draw_image_alt 0bfc (entry 33)
purpose: Returns at once if index >= count (u16 at 0). Entry i at 2+4i = (u16 image_offset, u16 mask_offset). Image = (u16 w, u16 h, rows in entry-22 planar layout, bpp = bpr/4 = ceil(w/8) bytes per plane row). Vertical clipping only: rows are clipped to y in [0,199], or to [config+0x1a, config+0x1c] (clip ymin/ymax, DGROUP 0x52d4/0x52d6) when config+0x0a (clip enable, 0x52c4) is nonzero; skipped source rows are advanced accordingly; no horizontal clipping. Destination = draw page. Page 0 (A000): opaque copy, bpp bytes per plane per row (map mask per plane); flags are ignored, and a nonzero mask offset must not be used on page 0 (the masked code path assumes page-1 addressing). Page 1, no mask, no mirror: copies bpp bytes per plane row; if w%8 != 0 the last byte is merged so pixels right of the image width keep their old value (mask table CS:0x252). Page 1 with mask (ITEMS/MON): mask rows are 1 bpp, ceil(w/8) bytes per row, MSB = leftmost, bit 1 = pixel is transparent (destination kept), bit 0 = take source: dest = (dest & m) | (src & ~m) per plane. Mirror (bit1): source bytes are bit-reversed through the CS:0x314 table and written right-to-left, so the image appears mirrored AND shifted one pixel left (source pixel px lands at dest x0+8*bpp-2-px); mirrored pixels are ORed into the destination (not replaced), and bit 0 of the byte immediately left of the image is cleared then set from the source's last pixel; with a mask the mask is mirrored the same way (dest &= mirrored mask; dest |= mirrored src & ~mask). Vertical flip (bit0): row step becomes -40 and the first destination row is y+h (row index y+h is looked up in the row table, so y+h must be <= 199), so the flipped image occupies rows y+1..y+h top-down reversed.
notes: The mirror/flip paths are exercised only by DUNGEON (walls drawn on page 1 then copied). Mask semantics verified against ITEMS.16/MON0.16 headers (mask size = h*ceil(w/8)).

name: draw_bitmap_white
inputs: AX=segment of a 1-bpp image file with u16 offsets (TITLE.BIT, BRITISH.BIT, PROPORT.PCS), BX=image index, SI=x (any pixel x; bit-shifted), DI=y
wrapper: draw_image_masked 1000:1044 (draw_stacked_pictures 0d72 for TITLE.BIT strips; INTRO 8b46; FONT e1e0 for PROPORT.PCS glyphs, index = char-0x20)
purpose: Table: u16 count, then u16 offset[i] at 2+2i; image = (u16 w, u16 h, h rows of w>>3 bytes, MSB = leftmost pixel; w must be a multiple of 8, extra pixels are dropped). Returns if index >= count. ALWAYS draws into PAGE 1 (ignores the draw page). For every 1 bit the pixel (x+i, y+row) is set to colour 15 (the bit is set in all four plane regions); 0 bits are transparent. No clipping; no bounds check on x+w.
notes: Name in root_part1 'draw_image_masked' is misleading: this is a transparent 1-bpp white sprite blit to page 1.

name: draw_tile
inputs: AL=col, AH=row (map view cells), BX=tile 0..511, CX=cell_w (8; x origin), DX=cell_h (8; y origin), SI=tile_w, DI=tile_h (both must be 16 or nothing is drawn)
wrapper: draw_tile 1000:10e0; also called internally by entry 32 (CF=1)
purpose: Opaque 16x16 blit of tile BX from the tile segment (CS:0x206, tile at BX*0x80 in the entry-24 layout) to pixel x = (CX & ~7) + 16*col, y = DX + 16*row (byte column = CX>>3 + 2*col). Honours the draw page (page 0: per-plane map-mask writes; page 1: plane regions). No clipping (col 0..10, row 0..10 expected).
notes: With the game's config (8,8) tile (c,r) lands at (8+16c, 8+16r): the 11x11 map view occupies pixels 8..183 x 8..183.

name: stub_28
inputs: none
purpose: Bare RETF (own stub at 3000:1634). Unused in EGA; CGA.DRV points entry 22 at its equivalent stub.

name: stub_29
inputs: none
purpose: Bare RETF stub (the shared stub used by entries 3,6,7,11,14,18,23,29).

name: free_tileset
inputs: none
purpose: If the tile segment CS:0x206 is nonzero, frees it with INT 21h AH=49h (ES=segment). CS:0x206 is NOT cleared, so a later tile draw would read freed memory until entry 24 is called again (the game always reloads TILES.16 before drawing tiles again).

name: draw_glyph
inputs: AX=cell column 0..39 (AH must be 0), BX=cell row 0..24, DL=fg colour, DH=bg colour, ES:DI=8 glyph bytes (one per row, MSB = left pixel; IBM.CH/RUNES.CH layout)
wrapper: put_char 1000:16ba (glyph temporarily modified by prepare_glyph for underline/inverse)
purpose: Opaque 8x8 character cell at pixels (8*AX, 8*BX): glyph bit 1 -> fg, bit 0 -> bg, all four planes rewritten. Honours the draw page (page 0: four masked write passes per row; page 1: writes ~glyph into bg planes / 0 into others, then ORs glyph into fg planes). No clipping. Side effect: clears CS:0x253d, the 'dissolve makes sound' flag (initial value 1), so entry 34 CF=0 is silent once any glyph has been drawn since the driver was loaded.

name: animate_tiles / draw_effect_frame
inputs: CF=0: animate_tiles (AX ignored; ROOT passes the IBM.CH font segment). CF=1: draw_effect_frame: AX=frame 0..16, SI=col, DI=row (map cells), BL=mode byte (0xFF -> base tile 0x44, else base tile 5), CX=cell_w, DX=cell_h
purpose: CF=0 mutates tile bitmaps in the tile segment (entry-24 layout; 'group' = 4 plane bytes of 8 pixels, 32 groups per tile; M(t) = the plane-3 byte of each group of tile t used as an 8-pixel mask applied to all 4 planes of the same group) using a private LCG seed CS:0x1f94 (init 0x7664): s=((s+0x9248) ror16 3) ^ 0x9248 + 0x11. Steps per call: (1) for each of the 32 groups g one random byte is written into tile 0x1e8 bytes g*4+1,+3; tile 0x1e9 g*4+0,+2,+3; tile 0x1ea g*4+2,+3; tile 0x1eb g*4+0,+3 (noise sprites). (2) tiles 1, 2, 3 and 0x8f: rows rotate down by one (row r -> r+1, row 15 -> row 0) (water animation). (3) for i=0..15: tile 0x60+i := (self & ~M(0x70+i)) | (tile 3 & M(0x70+i)) (shoreline tiles show animated water through the mask held in plane 3 of tiles 0x70..0x7f). (4) tile 0x108 := (self & ~M(0x100)) | (tile 0x1eb & M(0x100)); tile 0x1b4 := (self & ~M(0x100)) | (tile 0x1e9 & M(0x100)). (5) for i=0..3: tile 0x34+i := (self & ~M(0xd0+i)) | (tile 3 & M(0xd0+i)); tile 0xe4+i := (self & M(0xd0+i)) | (tile 3 & ~M(0xd0+i)) (plane 3 of tiles 0xd0..0xd3 is inverted and restored around it). (6) for i=0..3: tile 0xb0+i ^= (tile 0x1ea & tile 0xc0+i) and tile 0xbc+i ^= (tile 0x1ea & tile 0xcc+i) (byte-wise over all 128 bytes); tile 0xde ^= (tile 0x1eb & tile 0xc2) (flames). (7) depending on bits of the current seed: bit0: tile 0x12 rows 0<->2 swapped; bit1: tile 0x14 rows 2<->4 left half (bytes 0-3) only; bit2: tile 0x15 rows 0<->2; bit3: tile 0x3e rows 0<->2; bit4: tile 0x121 rows 1<->3 right half (bytes 4-7) only; bit5: tile 0x123 rows 1<->3; bit6: tile 0x12d rows 1<->3 right half; bit0 again: tile 0x12f rows 1<->3 (flickering flags/fires). CF=1: saves tile slot 0x116 (128 bytes), builds in it a copy of the base tile (5, or 0x44 when BL==0xFF) whose LAST `frame` rows (rows 16-frame..15) are replaced by the FIRST `frame` rows (0..frame-1) of tile 0xdc, draws slot 0x116 at cell (col,row) with entry 27 (honours draw page; CX/DX passed through), then restores slot 0x116. Callers step frame 15..1 with delays, so the 0xdc image slides downward out of the cell revealing the base tile.
notes: Mechanics are exact; which game objects the tile numbers are is not verified (1-3 = water, 0x1e8.. = noise/fire sprites).

name: draw_image_mirrored
inputs: same as entry 25; the stub ORs 2 into CL before jumping to entry 25
purpose: Entry 25 with the horizontal-mirror flag forced on: draws the image mirrored (and shifted one pixel left, ORed into the destination) - see entry 25. Only meaningful on page 1 (page 0 ignores the flag).

name: dissolve_rect / tile_dissolve_step
inputs: CF=0: AX=x1, BX=y1, CX=x2, DX=y2 (inclusive). CF=1: AX=col, BX=row (cells), SI=tile, CX=cell_w, DX=cell_h, DI=step 0..255
outputs: none (CF=0 returns early when a key is pending)
wrapper: rect_effect 1000:0f46 (CF=0; ENDGAME a290, BLCKTHRN aba0, SJOG c5c6, INTRO 830e/8770), tile_transition_effect 1000:1068 (CF=1, DI=0..255)
purpose: CF=0 (dissolve): reveals the rectangle of PAGE 1 on PAGE 0 one pixel at a time in pseudo-random order (always A000 <- A800, independent of the draw page). N=w*h, w=x2-x1+1, h=y2-y1+1; b = bit length of N-1; taps = table CS:0x254d[b-2] = {2:0x0003,3:0x0006,4:0x000c,5:0x0014,6:0x0030,7:0x0060,8:0x00b8,9:0x0110,10:0x0240,11:0x0500,12:0x0ca0,13:0x1b00,14:0x3500,15:0x6000,16:0xb400}; v=1; loop { x=v mod w, y=v div w; if y<h copy pixel (x1+x,y1+y) from page 1 to page 0 (all 4 planes); v>>=1; if the shifted-out bit was 1: v^=taps } until v==1; finally copy pixel (x1,y1). Sound: if CS:0x253d != 0 (true only until the first glyph is drawn by entry 31) every second copied pixel runs the noise routine FUN_27af (speaker gate on; PIT channel 2 reload = 1193182/f with f uniform in [100, CS:0x27a7/2] Hz; busy delay of (cpu_speed>>4) iterations; CS:0x27a7 starts at 240 and is incremented per call, so the pitch range widens) and checks INT 16h AH=1; a pending key aborts the dissolve (CF=1 from the helper), and the speaker is gated off at the end. CF=1 (tile dissolve step): draws exactly one pixel of tile SI at map cell (col,row) (pixel origin x=(CX&~7)+16*col, y=DX+16*row) on PAGE 0 (always A000): step 0 -> tile pixel (0,0); step 1 resets the 8-bit LFSR state CS:0x2541 to 1; for step>=1: v=state, pixel (x=v>>4, y=v&15) is copied from the tile, then state = (v>>1) ^ (v&1 ? 0xB8 : 0). Calling with DI=0,1,...,255 draws every pixel exactly once.
notes: Port: implement the LFSR orders exactly if the look should match; sound only matters before the first text is printed (title/intro).

name: title_fire_frame / title_fire_dissolve
inputs: CF=0: none. CF=1: AX=segment of the decompressed WD.BIT (1-bpp 288x49 mask: u16 count=1, u16 offset=4, u16 w=288, u16 h=49, then 49 rows of 36 bytes starting at byte 8)
wrapper: direct from INTRO: FUN_1000_a250 (wait_ticks(1) then CLC) and FUN_1000_a26e (STC, AX=arg)
purpose: Assumes INTRO has drawn the four 288x49 fire frames of ULTIMA.16 (images 1..4) into page 1 at rows 0, 50, 100, 150 (x offset 16). CF=0: copies 49 full-width rows of page 1 starting at row 50*k (k = CS:0x282b, cycles 0,1,2,3 after each call) to page 0 rows 65..113 (next animation frame). CF=1: allocates a 32000-byte DOS block (FUN_0414), saves page 1 into it, clears page 1, then dissolves the frames back in: LFSR state v (14-bit, taps 0x3500, start 1): y=v div 288, x=v mod 288; if y<49 and (pass 1: mask bit (x,y) of WD.BIT is 0; pass 2: always) the pixel (x+16, y+50*k) for k=0..3 is restored into page 1 from the saved copy (all 4 planes); every 128 pixels (256 when cpu_speed < 250) it shows the next frame on screen (the CF=0 body), then if (rand16 & 0x1ff) < CS:0x28c4 (starts 400, -3 per frame) plays a crackle (FUN_27af with f in [100,1500] Hz, 25 units) and busy-waits 45 x cpu_speed, else waits 50 x cpu_speed; after each pixel INT 16h AH=1 is polled and a pending key aborts both passes. When v returns to 1 the pixel (0,0) is done and the pass ends. Finally page 1 is fully restored from the saved block (so after an abort the caller still has all four frames) and the block is freed. The private LCG seed CS:0x28c2 (init 0x7664) uses the same formula as entry 32.
notes: Visual: the burning title on the intro screen fades in from nothing while the flames animate; sound = speaker crackle. Called twice from INTRO with CF=1 (a26e) and repeatedly with CF=0 (a250).

name: tile_patch
inputs: AX=command 0..4; command 2: BL=hour 0..23, BH=minute 0..59 (ROOT 71aa loads BL from 0x587f and BH from 0x5881)
purpose: All commands edit the tile segment (entry-24 layout). 0: saves row 14 (8 bytes) of tiles 0xc8 and 0x117 into driver buffers (CS:0x2aa3/0x2aab) and overwrites each with that tile's row 0. 1: restores both saved rows. 2 (clock): in tiles 0xfa and 0xfb clears the 3x3 ring around pixel (8,3) - pixels (7,2),(8,2),(9,2),(7,3),(9,3),(7,4),(8,4),(9,4) - in planes 0,1,3 only (plane 2 is left set, so a cleared hand pixel becomes colour 4 = red, the face colour; the centre (8,3) is untouched), then sets one white pixel (all 4 planes) for the hour hand at ring position hour mod 12 and one for the minute hand at position minute/5, positions 0..11 -> (8,2),(9,2),(9,2),(9,3),(9,4),(9,4),(8,4),(7,4),(7,4),(7,3),(7,2),(7,2). 3: swaps plane bytes 1 and 2 of every group (i.e. exchanges colour bits 1 and 2: 2<->4, 3<->5, 10<->12, 11<->13) in tiles 5, 0x1e, 0x1f, 0x4c, 0xca, 0x20..0x26, 0x30..0x37, 0x60..0x6f; an involution. 4: converts the whole 64 KB tile set back to packed nibbles, remaps the nibbles of tiles 0x44, 0x5c, 0x5d, 0x90, 0x92, 0x94, 0x96, 0x9b, 0xab, 0xac, 0xaf, 0xb0, 0xb1, 0xbf, 0xdc, 0x108, 0x10e, 0x11a, 0x138, 0x139, 0x13a, 0x13b through the colour map {0:0,1:5,2:4,3:4,4:2,5:1,6:2,7:7,8:8,9:12,10:12,11:12,12:10,13:9,14:14,15:15}, then re-converts everything to planar (not reversible).
notes: Command 4 used by ENDGAME, 3 by DNGLOOK (b3c0), 0/1 around dungeon-room combat, 2 by pass_time in towns.

name: set_speed_and_play_title_zoom
inputs: AX=CPU speed factor (g_cpu_speed 0x5356: busy-loop iterations per 55 ms tick * 18 / 750)
outputs: AX=1 if a key was pressed during the animation (key consumed via INT 21h AH=06h), else 0
wrapper: driver_set_speed 1000:1140 - only caller is draw_stacked_pictures 0d72 (INTRO title screen)
purpose: Stores AX at CS:0x1c1e; this is the delay unit for EVERY busy-wait in the driver (this routine, the dissolve clicks of entry 34, entry 35), and it stays 0 (= 65536-iteration loops) until this entry is first called. Then plays the title zoom: draw_stacked_pictures has put the 7 TITLE.BIT strips (heights N = 3,7,11,20,32,45,61, widths 24..280, centred horizontally) into page 1 at rows A = 0,3,10,21,41,73,118 (cumulative heights). For stage k=0..6 the driver copies strip rows from page 1 (plane-0 region) to page 0 with SEQ map mask 09h, i.e. only planes 0 and 3 are written (the strip appears in colour 9, light blue, on a black background; planes 1,2 are never touched) into a band of N rows at B = 75,72,71,66,60,53,46 (all centred on row ~76). Even stages are drawn top-down from row B; odd stages bottom-up from row B+N with ascending source rows, i.e. vertically mirrored. A stage is a scripted sequence (tables at CS:0x1e8c, format per stage: u8 A, u8 B, u8 N, u8 L, then L bytes = row indices separated by 0xFF group terminators): the 'show' phase reads the table backwards from the end, marking each listed row visible and running one render pass per 0xFF (7 passes); the 'hide' phase (skipped after the last stage) reads it forwards from byte 1, clearing rows and rendering per 0xFF (6 passes). A render pass = delay 12*speed iterations, then in the band: clear floor(hidden/2) rows (planes 0,3 zeroed), draw the visible rows packed consecutively, clear the remaining rows - so the visible rows always sit centred in the band and the strip grows/shrinks about its middle. INT 21h AH=06h is polled after every row; a key aborts: the full-size strip (A=118,B=46,N=61) is drawn at once and AX=1 is returned. GC registers are reset at exit.
notes: Script bytes CS:0x1e8c..0x1f93 are reproduced in driver_api.md. The exact visual (flip/zoom) has not been checked in DOSBox.
